title: Depth: conventions and core's depth nodes

questions.q: Which end is white in DA3Render's depth and MoGeRender's depth?
options: Near in DA3, far in MoGe
questions.why: normalize_depth_v2_style inverts so that near is 1, and _normalize_disparity uses 1/depth, which is largest close up.

questions.q: In a 2 m to 10 m scene, why is 6 m much darker on MoGe's render than on v2_style?
options: MoGe's grey is linear in 1/depth, so most of the range goes on close distances
questions.answer: MoGe's grey is linear in 1/depth, so most of the range goes on close distances
questions.why: The lab gives 0.167 against 0.500 at 6 m. Same scene, a different scale.

questions.q: A depth map looks flat and pale everywhere. What is the most likely cause, from the lab?
options: The ControlNet strength is too low
A far outlier, such as sky, took up the range
questions.answer: A far outlier, such as sky, took up the range
questions.why: With min_max, 0.5% of pixels at 500 m leaves the scene 5 of 256 grey levels.

questions.q: What does LotusConditioning take as input?
options: Nothing: it returns a fixed conditioning
questions.answer: Nothing: it returns a fixed conditioning
questions.why: The node has no inputs. A comment in the source says Lotus uses null conditioning, so its result is inlined.

questions.q: You have a depth map but aren't sure of its convention. What is the quick check?
options: Run a full render at strength 2
See whether something you know is near is brighter than something you know is far
questions.answer: See whether something you know is near is brighter than something you know is far
questions.why: ImageInvert turns one convention into the other exactly, so a look decides if you need it.
